question: vertical-channels
summary: Each target vertical (law, insurance, property management, food, trades) has a state association that sells access to its members at a published price, and the cheapest, closest doors are in New Brunswick: the NJSBA Solo and Small-Firm Conference (Feb 20-21, at the New Jersey Law Center) sells an exhibitor table for $500 and includes an opt-in attendee list, and the NJSBA Family Law Symposium (Jan 23-24, Hyatt Regency New Brunswick) sells a Saturday table for $1,800. On the vendor side, insurance and property management charge modest annual associate dues (Big I NJ $400/year for technology providers; CAI-NJ $685 business partner; NJAA supplier partner $650) but NJAA bars non-member vendors from its Conference & Expo entirely, so membership is a prerequisite, not an option. Food and trades are the most expensive doors: NJRHA vendor memberships run $2,500-$12,500 and NJ ACCA associate sponsor tiers $1,750-$14,000, while the NJ Food Council publishes no dues at all and only lets current members sponsor. The practical sequence is to buy the low-cost association memberships plus one or two local legal exhibits first, and defer the $2,500+ food/trades packages until a paid pilot is funding them.

findings.finding: The single best-fit, lowest-cost channel is the NJSBA Solo and Small-Firm Conference, held at the New Jersey Law Center in New Brunswick, and it sells exhibitor tables from $500 with an opt-in attendee list included. (The short drive from Milltown is an inference from the venue city, not a figure stated in the source.)
findings.evidence: The 2026 sponsor form lists Bronze Exhibitor $500 (two exhibitor badges for Saturday, one table in the exhibit area assigned first-come, recognition on pre-event marketing, and 'List of attendees who have opted in to having their information shared'), Silver $1,000 (also named sponsor of Saturday lunch at the Law Center and two Friday dinner tickets) and Gold $2,000 (named sponsor of Friday dinner at Cuzin's Seafood in New Brunswick, Saturday lunch and Saturday evening cocktail party, two dinner tickets, two badges, one table). The conference is dated 'Feb, 20 - 21 | New Jersey Law Center, New Brunswick', with programming on February 21 and a wine-and-cheese networking reception at the end of the day.

findings.finding: The NJSBA Family Law Symposium is a second, also-local legal event with a Saturday-only exhibitor table at $1,800, held at the Hyatt Regency in New Brunswick; its 2026 form does not mention an attendee list.
findings.evidence: The 2026 exhibitor form reads '2026 FAMILY LAW SYMPOSIUM January 23 - 24 Hyatt Regency, New Brunswick', with options 'Main Room: Friday and Saturday ... $2,000' (no exhibiting Friday, but sponsors at that level are invited to the Friday evening cocktail party) and 'Saturday only ... $1,800'. Each table is one 6' skirted table with two chairs; set-up Saturday begins at 7 a.m. No attendee-list benefit appears on any tier of this form.

findings.finding: The NJSBA Annual Meeting is the highest-reach legal event in the state (about 3,000 attendees) and a booth costs $2,000, but legal-tech vendors already crowd that hall, so differentiation matters more than presence.
findings.evidence: The 2026 prospectus says the meeting 'sees some 3,000 attorneys, judges, and other legal professionals over the three-day event', May 13-15 at the Borgata, Atlantic City. An 8'x10' booth is $2,000 with a $200 per-corner premium; the fee includes pipe and drape, a 6' draped table and two chairs, one 110V/20A outlet, a program/app listing and a post-conference attendee list. Exhibit hall hours are Wednesday May 13, 10:30 a.m.-5:30 p.m. and Thursday May 14, 9:30 a.m.-3:30 p.m. The previous-exhibitor list includes Anytime AI, DRai Solutions, eMazzanti Technologies, Esquire Digital, Clio, Smokeball, PracticePanther, LEAP and FindLaw.

findings.finding: You cannot join the state bar association as a non-lawyer consultant; the NJSBA application only admits NJ-bar attorneys, attorneys of other state bars, and legal-professional categories such as paralegals and legal administrators - so the only door is exhibitor/sponsor.
findings.evidence: The 2026 application's categories are Regular Membership (NJ bar, admitted year), Associate Membership ('I am a member of the Bar in the state of ___'), and Law and Legal Professional Membership (legal administrator, law librarian, paralegal/legal assistant, law student). Dues for an attorney admitted 2020 or prior are $295 (government/non-profit $225); the Solo and Small Firm section is $50. NJSBA estimates 10% of dues is non-deductible because of lobbying.

findings.finding: Big I New Jersey explicitly invites technology vendors into associate membership for $400 a year, which buys directory visibility, committee seats and member pricing rather than a booth.
findings.evidence: The associate membership page says companies 'affiliated with the insurance industry and/or interested in promoting the purposes and objectives of the association' are eligible, including 'agency management system service providers, technology service providers'. Benefits: listing in the online associate member directory that independent agents search, logo on the BigINJ.org home page, ability to serve on committees and task forces, member pricing on events and education, up to five newsletter subscriptions, and the option to run for one of two Associate Member-At-Large board seats. 'Associate members' dues are $400 and renew each calendar year', prorated 50% for July-October joiners; November-December joiners pay full dues but do not renew until the following year.

findings.finding: Big I NJ's annual agents conference already gives technology providers dedicated floor space ('Tech Row') and teaches agents about AI errors-and-omissions risk - the exact conversation an AI agent vendor wants to be adjacent to.
findings.evidence: The 2026 NJ Agents Conference ran October 18-20 at Mount Airy Casino Resort & Spa, with a 'NEW TECH ROW' during Sunday's cocktail reception and Monday morning where 'Representatives from each company will be available to showcase their product'. Monday 8:00-10:00 a.m. was 'MANAGING E&O RISK IN THE AGE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE', presented by Nick Johnson of Ataviz, approved for 2 NJCE credits, covering AI use cases, liability exposures, vendor vetting, contract provisions and agency procedures. Tech Row participants listed were Catalyit, ACORD, ACORD Solutions Group, Bind AI and ClientCircle.

findings.finding: Big I NJ's published agency dues schedule is banded by agency revenue, from $680 (under $100,000) to $3,955 (over $11 million) - so a small agency principal's association commitment is in the hundreds, not thousands, of dollars; the schedule itself is still headed 2018-2019, so treat the levels as provisional.
findings.evidence: The new-member application's 'Dues Information' table gives 'Code / Total Revenue, Including Branches / Annual Membership Dues': A <$100,000 $680; B $100,001-$250,000 $780; C $250,001-$500,000 $950; D $500,001-$1 mil $1200; E $1,000,001-$3 mil $1380; F $3,000,001-$4 mil $1755; G $4,000,001-$5 mil $2015; H $5,000,001-$6 mil $2280; I $6,000,001-$7 mil $2595; J $7,000,001-$8 mil $2855; K $8,000,001-$9 mil $3150; L $9,000,001-$10 mil $3415; M $10,000,001-$11 mil $3680; N >$11 mil $3955. The same document says membership then ran 'through August 31, 2019' and puts the estimated non-deductible (lobbying) portion of dues for 2018-2019 at 20.90%, which is why the levels are cited as provisional rather than current.

findings.finding: Big I NJ agency members are offered concrete offsets (conference discounts, marketing reimbursements) and run on a September 1 fiscal year, which shows how much discretionary spend a small agency principal already directs through the association.
findings.evidence: The agency membership page lists savings: '$80 average commission for one RLI Policy', '12% average commissions through Big I Markets', 'Up to $1500 in reimbursements from the Marketing Reimbursement Program (MRP)', '30% savings on continuing education programs' and '40% savings on NJ Agents Conference registrations'. The association runs a September 1 fiscal year, with mid-year proration of 1/3 off (December-February) and 2/3 off (March-May). The page itself publishes no dollar dues figure.

findings.finding: The property-management vertical (NJAA) hard-gates vendor access to its Conference & Expo: non-member suppliers cannot attend at all, so a supplier membership is the entry ticket.
findings.evidence: The 2026 Conference & Expo registration page states, under 'Non-Exhibiting Supplier Partners', that the level 'is for NJAA Supplier Partners that are unable to purchase a booth. Non-member suppliers / vendors cannot attend this event'. The same page gives management-level registration as $475 for NJAA members and $625 for non-members, with 'Rates increase Friday, May 1, 2026'.

findings.finding: NJAA supplier partner dues are $650 a year plus a $25 processing fee, including one free classified in the online directory.
findings.evidence: The membership information page prices supplier partner dues at '$650' annually including one free classified in NJAA's online directory, plus a $25 processing fee; joiners after July 1 pay a prorated $312.50 and then full dues of $625 the following year. Additional classifieds are $50 each and a website hyperlink in the directory is $250.

findings.finding: NJAA's Conference & Expo sells inexpensive single-item sponsorships ($500-$750) that are cheaper than a booth, but the full brochure and booth pricing sit behind a member log-in.
findings.evidence: The 2026 sponsorship PDF prices 'Networking Lunch on the Tradeshow Floor (4 Available) $750', 'Expo Floor Cocktail Reception (72 Available) $750' (marked exhibitor only) and 'Breakfast (Wednesday) (3 Available) $500', each with signage/logo recognition and listing in pre-event and post-event communications. The sponsorships web page says a brochure 'outlines every opportunity available for the 2026 NJAA Conference & Expo, including benefits, pricing, and visibility details' and that 'NJAA log-in and password required to view and purchase'.

findings.finding: CAI-NJ is the cheapest formal vendor seat in property management at $685 a year, and the application confirms how that total is built.
findings.evidence: The 2026 CAI Business Partner application totals dues as 'Membership Fee $660' + 'Advocacy Support Fee $25' = 'Total Membership Dues $685' (optional $25 Foundation donation makes $710); $39 of dues is for the non-refundable Common Ground subscription and CAI estimates 17% of dues is non-deductible. It also states 'Membership in a local chapter is included in your membership.'

findings.finding: CAI-NJ business partners get one free printed-directory category but must pay separately for the online directory, and prior-year exhibitors are contacted first about keeping the same Conference & Expo booth.
findings.evidence: The chapter FAQ says all members current as of January 1 are in that year's printed directory at no charge and that 'Business partners receive one category listed at no charge. However, they can expand their listing in additional categories for a nominal fee.' It adds that the online directory 'is an additional paid service reserved only for members', and that 'exhibitors of the previous year will all be contacted first regarding booking the same booth that they had for the upcoming Conference & Expo.' Caveat: the booth-sale schedule printed beside that answer still shows 2020 dates, so the FAQ text is at least partly dated.

findings.finding: CAI-NJ's monthly magazine is an unusually cheap way to stay in front of community managers: a member eighth-page ad is $139 and a quarter page $205.
findings.evidence: The 2026 Community Trends rate sheet (member rates) lists per-issue prices of $660 full page, $535 three-quarter, $370 half, $288 third, $205 quarter and $139 eighth for 12x/6x advertisers, and separately for the October Conference & Expo issue only: $983 full, $818 three-quarter, $653 half, $570 third, $488 quarter, $405 eighth. Deadlines are the 15th of the prior month; the publication is fully electronic and ads 'click and link' to the advertiser's website; non-member rates are quoted on request.

findings.finding: Restaurants are the most expensive association door measured here: NJRHA vendor membership starts at $2,500 a year, five times the CAI-NJ or Big I NJ associate rate, and roughly five times what an operator pays.
findings.evidence: NJRHA's 'Vendor Membership Opportunities' page lists three tiers - 'Maitre D' $2,500', 'Chef's Table $5,000', 'Executive Suite $12,500' - each a one-year membership including logo use, vendor directory listing, newsletter and advocacy updates and a newsletter welcome listing; the tiers add 2/3/4 newsletter sponsorships, 1/2/4 event tickets, 1/2/4 custom eblasts, 1/2/4 social posts, with the member list and an event sponsorship at the $5,000 level, and 'Host & Record Educational Webinar' plus 'Brand Exposure at all NJRHA Events' only at $12,500. For contrast, the association's operator page prices a Restaurant membership at $450 for one location, '+$100 per additional location'.

findings.finding: For food businesses, the NJ Food Council's event calendar is concentrated within about 20 minutes of Milltown, and its Holiday Reception is in East Brunswick.
findings.evidence: The Council's events page lists the 2026 Holiday Reception & Retirement Celebration on Wednesday, December 9, 2026, 5:00-8:00 p.m. at Park Chateau Estate & Gardens, East Brunswick; the 2026 Night of Distinction on May 20, 2026 at The Palace at Somerset Park; the 2026 Annual Summer Golf Outing on August 17, 2026 at Forsgate Country Club, Monroe; and the 2026 Trade Relations Conference & Golf Outing on April 14-15, 2026 at Caesars Atlantic City. (The 'about 20 minutes from Milltown' framing is an inference from those towns, not a source figure.)

findings.finding: The NJ Food Council publishes no dues on its sponsorship page and only lets existing members buy sponsor status, so the consultancy cannot simply buy visibility.
findings.evidence: The 'Become a Sponsor' page states 'Current members of the NJ Food Council are eligible to elevate their membership to a Sponsor level.' Benefits listed: registrations to the Annual Meeting, Night of Distinction, Trade Relations Conference and Annual Golf Outing, company recognition in the weekly News & Views newsletter, logo on the website, event programs, special acknowledgment at events and the company name on a banner at each major event. No dollar figures appear on the page.

findings.finding: The trades have a separate, affordable state HVAC association (NJ ACCA) whose contractor dues are $239-$449, distinct from national ACCA's $775-$5,150 tiers; vendor access is sold as associate sponsorship from $1,750 to $14,000.
findings.evidence: NJ ACCA's contractor page lists 'Business Membership for Contractors ($449/year)' covering everyone in the organization and 'Individual Membership for Contractors ($239/year)' for one person, and states 'NJ ACCA and ACCA are separate but affiliated organizations. Membership in one does not automatically grant membership in the other.' Its associate (supplier) sheet (njacca.memberclicks.net/assets/Membership/2026%20NJ%20ACCA%20Associate%20Memberships.pdf) lists five levels: $14,000 (up to 2 tickets per meeting, logo, company profile, press releases, promotional content, dinner sponsor, tee sign, event signage, speaking opportunity, 4 golfers), $10,000, $5,000 (2 tickets per year), $2,500, $1,750 (logo on website, event signage).

findings.finding: Independent agents get a dedicated trade show plus two AI/technology sessions at the PIANJ/PIANY annual conference, so a single June trip covers both state agent audiences.
findings.evidence: The posted conference schedule runs Sunday June 7 to Tuesday June 9 with the trade show open Sunday 4-6:30 p.m. (with cash giveaway and networking reception) and Monday 9 a.m.-noon and 1:45-4 p.m. (bloody mary/mimosa bar, wine and cheese reception, exhibitor door prizes and grand door-prize drawing). Sessions include 'Technology: Impacting You and Your Clients' (John Fear, Monday 8-10 a.m.) and 'Deep Dive Live-AI/Cyber' (Monday 2-3:30 p.m.).

findings.finding: National ACCA's contractor dues run $775-$5,150 a year, and its own conference is a March trip to National Harbor rather than a local play.
findings.evidence: The tier pages state 'Investment: $775/yr' (Bronze, 10% member discount on events and courses), 'Investment: $1,850/yr' (Silver, 20% discount, '$900' ACCA Bucks, 20% ComfortU discount) and 'Investment: $5,150/yr' (Gold, 30% discount, '$2500' ACCA Bucks, ComfortU 'Unlimited Included'). The events page lists 'ACCA 2027, March 10-12, 2027 | Washington D.C. - National Harbor'.

findings.finding: The Middlesex County Chamber is explicitly event-driven and sells event sponsorships rather than booths, but publishes no price list - it is a relationship channel, not a lead-buy.
findings.evidence: The chamber's sponsorship page says 'We are an event-driven Chamber because we believe in the power of personal networking to grow your business' and lists monthly committee meetings, targeted introductions, special interest groups and signature networking gatherings as the formats, with benefits described only qualitatively (brand recognition, connections, publicity) and no dollar figures.

resources.name: NJSBA Solo and Small-Firm Conference - exhibitor and sponsorship form
resources.what_it_offers: A table in the exhibit area at the New Jersey Law Center, New Brunswick, plus the opt-in attendee list; Bronze includes two Saturday badges and a table, Silver adds Saturday lunch sponsorship and two Friday dinner tickets, Gold adds Friday dinner and Saturday cocktail party naming.
resources.how_to_use_it: Email sponsorship@njsba.com or mail the form to NJSBA, Attn: Denisse Salinas, One Constitution Square, New Brunswick, NJ 08901; ask for the 2027 form in November-December 2026 since the 2026 event was February 20-21.

resources.name: NJSBA Family Law Symposium - exhibitor table
resources.what_it_offers: One 6' skirted table with two chairs at the Hyatt Regency, New Brunswick, with Friday cocktail-party access at the higher tier. The 2026 form lists no attendee list, so confirm whether one is included.
resources.cost: Saturday only $1,800; Friday and Saturday $2,000 (2026 form)
resources.how_to_use_it: Contact Paula Saha, 732-214-8509, sponsorship@njsba.com; the 2026 event was January 23-24, so request 2027 pricing in late 2026.

resources.name: NJSBA Annual Meeting and Convention - exhibit booth
resources.what_it_offers: 8'x10' booth at the Borgata, Atlantic City, with pipe and drape, table, two chairs, one electrical outlet, program/app listing and the post-conference attendee list; roughly 3,000 legal professionals attend.
resources.cost: $2,000 per booth; $200 per corner premium; digital signage add-on $500 (2026 prospectus)
resources.how_to_use_it: Book through exhibit manager dLPLAN (609-344-1333, njsba@dlplan.com); applications after the December deadline require full payment, and sponsorship add-ons go through sponsorship@njsba.com. The 2027 dates were not yet posted on the NJSBA site as of this research.

resources.name: Big I New Jersey associate membership (technology providers)
resources.what_it_offers: Directory listing agents search, logo on the home page, committee and task-force seats, member pricing on events and education, up to five newsletter subscriptions, eligibility for Associate Member-At-Large board seats.
resources.cost: $400 per calendar year; 50% prorated for July-October joins; November-December joins are full rate but renew the following year
resources.how_to_use_it: Contact Maria Keegan, mkeegan@biginj.org; join in November-December 2026 so the $400 carries through to the following year, then use the directory and committee seat to get onto the next NJ Agents Conference Tech Row.

resources.name: Big I NJ NJ Agents Conference (Tech Row)
resources.what_it_offers: Two-day agents conference with a dedicated technology-provider showcase, an AI/E&O class carrying 2 NJCE credits, golf and networking; the 2026 venue was Mount Airy Casino Resort & Spa, Pennsylvania, room rate $119.
resources.cost: Not public on the page (registration closed at time of research); member agencies get 40% off conference registrations per the membership page
resources.how_to_use_it: Ask Big I NJ about Tech Row participation for the 2027 edition (sponsorship contact listed on their sponsorships page: Jennifer Kacmarsky, 609-587-4333). Treat October 2027 as the target.

resources.name: CAI-NJ Business Partner membership
resources.what_it_offers: National CAI membership with New Jersey as the primary chapter, one free printed-directory category, paid online-directory listing, magazine and event visibility options, and the right to buy Conference & Expo booths (prior exhibitors contacted first).
resources.cost: $685 total ($660 membership + $25 mandatory advocacy support fee); $710 with the optional $25 foundation donation
resources.how_to_use_it: Apply through cainj.org/join-renew or caionline.org/join; membership questions to Robin Surgent, (609) 588-0030, robin@cainj.org. Ask about the 2027 Partnership Program tiers and booth-only pricing at the same time.

resources.name: CAI-NJ Community Trends advertising
resources.what_it_offers: Full-color ad in the chapter magazine (mostly electronic, clickable to your site), with a printed October Conference & Expo issue distributed to attendees.
resources.cost: Member per-issue rates $139 (1/8 page) to $660 (full page); October Conference & Expo issue $405 (1/8) to $983 (full)
resources.how_to_use_it: Email info@brainerdcommunications.com; deadline is the 15th of the prior month. Start with an eighth- or quarter-page in the October issue to test response.

resources.name: NJAA Supplier Partner membership
resources.what_it_offers: The only route for a vendor to attend NJAA's Conference & Expo, plus one free classified in the online directory; members-only events, education and publications.
resources.cost: $650 annual dues plus a $25 processing fee; after July 1 prorated to $312.50, with $625 full dues the following year; extra classifieds $50, directory hyperlink $250
resources.how_to_use_it: Join through njaa.com/membership-information (Supplier Partner link) or membership@njaa.com, 732-992-0600; then ask for the Conference & Expo exhibitor contract and sponsorship brochure, which require an NJAA log-in to view or purchase.

resources.name: NJAA Conference & Expo single-item sponsorships
resources.what_it_offers: Named sponsorship of breakfast, the tradeshow-floor networking lunch or the expo-floor cocktail reception, with signage, verbal acknowledgment and pre/post-event promotion.
resources.cost: Breakfast $500 (3 available); Networking Lunch $750 (4 available); Expo Floor Cocktail Reception $750 (72 available, exhibitor only) - 2026 rates
resources.how_to_use_it: Download the sponsorship brochure through the member portal or email membership@njaa.com; ask whether a booth is required to buy the lunch or breakfast item.

resources.name: NJRHA vendor membership
resources.what_it_offers: Year-round vendor listing and visibility to New Jersey restaurant and hospitality operators: directory listing, newsletter sponsorships, event tickets, custom eblasts and social posts, and at the top tier a hosted educational webinar and brand exposure at all NJRHA events.
resources.cost: Maitre D' $2,500; Chef's Table $5,000; Executive Suite $12,500 per year
resources.how_to_use_it: Email astone@njrha.org (address published on the vendor page) for the vendor application; compare against operator dues of $450 for one restaurant location, +$100 per additional location (njrha.org/join-today), before committing, and consider a single event sponsorship instead.

resources.name: NJRHA / NJ Restaurant Educational Foundation ProStart Invitational sponsorships
resources.what_it_offers: Access to a culinary-competition audience of about 150 attendees, with display tables, signage, chef-coat logos and newsletter/social recognition depending on tier.
resources.cost: Team Sponsor $500; Event Sponsor $1,000; Gold $2,500; Premier $5,000
resources.how_to_use_it: Contact Austin Morgan, amorgan@njrha.org; the 2026 event was February 25 at the Driscoll Foods Showroom - a low-cost way to meet operators and educators before buying a vendor membership.

resources.name: NJ ACCA associate (supplier) membership
resources.what_it_offers: Access to NJ HVACR contractors through statewide and North/South membership meetings, a membership database, newsletter logo and spotlight, golf outing, and a chance to present at a meeting or webinar at the higher tiers.
resources.how_to_use_it: Apply through the NJ ACCA membership form (njacca.memberclicks.net); use the lowest tier first for logo and event signage, and ask specifically about the 'Opportunity to present at Membership Meeting or Webinar' as the real trust-builder.

resources.name: NJ ACCA contractor membership (for context and referral partners)
resources.what_it_offers: Weekly newsletters, members-only events, discounted meetings and training, discounted health insurance via Association Member Trust, one surety bond per organization, and statehouse advocacy.
resources.how_to_use_it: Use this page to understand contractor priorities and to identify the contractors most likely to buy phone/intake automation; join as an associate rather than as a contractor.

resources.name: NJ Food Council events and sponsorship
resources.what_it_offers: The Council's calendar of buyer-heavy events - Annual Membership Meeting, Night of Distinction, Trade Relations Conference and Golf Outing, Summer Golf Outing, Holiday Reception, Mid-Atlantic Loss Prevention Conference - with sponsor recognition across all of them.
resources.cost: Membership dues not published; sponsorship available only as an elevation of current membership and unpriced on the page (contact 609-392-8899 or njfc@njfoodcouncil.com)
resources.how_to_use_it: Attend the December 9, 2026 Holiday Reception at Park Chateau in East Brunswick as a guest to gauge fit, and ask for the Associate membership application and sponsor rate card before paying anything.

resources.name: PIANJ / PIANY Annual Conference trade show
resources.what_it_offers: Exhibitor exposure to New Jersey and New York independent agents across two trade-show days within a three-day conference (Sunday afternoon and Monday), plus technology and AI/cyber education sessions that frame the buyer's problem.
resources.cost: Not public on the schedule page
resources.how_to_use_it: Check pia.org/events/conf/nynj for exhibitor pricing and the next cycle (the posted schedule ran June 7-9); one trip covers both state agent audiences.

resources.name: Middlesex County Chamber event sponsorships
resources.what_it_offers: Sponsorship of an event-driven calendar (monthly committees, targeted introductions, special interest groups, signature networking gatherings) reaching local business owners, professionals and civic figures.
resources.cost: Not public on the sponsorship page
resources.how_to_use_it: Request the sponsorship menu and event calendar by phone; prioritize a small event where you can speak rather than a logo placement, and use it for local credibility with Milltown-area businesses.

resources.name: ACCA 2027 (national HVAC conference) and national contractor tiers
resources.what_it_offers: National HVACR contractor education and networking, March 10-12, 2027 at National Harbor, Washington D.C., with contractor membership tiers from $775 to $5,150 a year.
resources.cost: Membership: Bronze $775/yr, Silver $1,850/yr, Gold $5,150/yr (acca.org/join/contractor-membership/bronze, /silver, /gold); conference registration not public on the events page
resources.how_to_use_it: Deprioritize for year one: the same buyers are reachable at NJ ACCA meetings for a fraction of the travel cost, and membership in NJ ACCA does not grant national ACCA access.

recommendations_for_us: Inference: sequence the spend as legal first, insurance second, property third, food/trades last. The evidence is price and proximity: NJSBA's New Brunswick events are $500-$2,000, Big I NJ associate membership is $400, CAI-NJ is $685 and NJAA is $650, while NJRHA vendor tiers start at $2,500 and NJ ACCA associate tiers at $1,750 - so three verticals can be entered for roughly the price of one food membership.

Inference: buy the NJSBA Solo and Small-Firm Conference Bronze table ($500) for the February 2027 edition as the first paid move, because it is the only channel found that combines a small-firm-only audience, a physical table, a stated opt-in attendee list and an in-state venue; upgrade to Silver ($1,000) only after a pilot is signed, since the extra $500 buys lunch sponsorship naming rather than more leads.

Inference: join Big I NJ as an associate ($400) in November or December 2026, because the page states November-December joiners pay full dues but do not renew until the following year - effectively 13-14 months for $400 - and then ask for Tech Row placement at the 2027 NJ Agents Conference, where agents are already being taught AI/E&O risk and are therefore pre-sold on the problem.

Inference: treat NJAA membership ($650 plus $25 processing) as a prerequisite purchase, not a marketing experiment, because the registration page says non-member suppliers and vendors cannot attend the Conference & Expo at all; do not send anyone to that show without the membership in hand.

Inference: lead with the compliance-and-liability framing rather than 'AI agents'. Two independent association programs now teach this framing to these buyers - Big I NJ's 2-credit AI/E&O class and PIANJ's 'Deep Dive Live - AI/Cyber' and 'Technology: Impacting You and Your Clients' sessions - which suggests the fastest trust path is a 30-minute talk on AI intake risk, call recording consent and vendor vetting, not a product demo.

Inference: ask for the opt-in attendee list at every legal event, but expect it only where it is written down. The Solo and Small-Firm form lists it at all three tiers; the Family Law Symposium's 2026 form does not mention it at any tier, so confirm before treating that $1,800 table as a list-buy. Build the follow-up sequence before paying, since a table without follow-up converts nothing.

Inference: use CAI-NJ's cheapest print unit ($139-$205 per issue) as a low-risk test of manager interest before considering any partnership tier; the rate card makes this the lowest-cost way to appear repeatedly in front of community managers.

Inference: for restaurants and food businesses, attend the NJ Food Council Holiday Reception on December 9, 2026 in East Brunswick as a guest and buy a single NJRHA event sponsorship (ProStart starts at $500) rather than a $2,500 vendor membership, because neither association publishes evidence that vendor spend converts to small-operator sales, and NJ Food Council sponsorship is not even purchasable without membership first.

Inference: for trades, work through NJ ACCA rather than national ACCA, because the state chapter sells a $1,750 entry point with event signage and a newsletter spotlight while national ACCA contractor dues run $775-$5,150 and its conference is in Maryland in March.

Inference: budget the association memberships off a small agency's actual dues band, not a guess: Big I NJ's published schedule puts an agency under $100,000 revenue at $680 a year, which is the same order of magnitude as the $400 vendor seat you would buy - so an agency principal is not committing thousands to the association, and a five-figure vendor package is unlikely to match their own spending habits.

Inference: plan the calendar around published dates - Dec 9, 2026 (NJ Food Council, East Brunswick), January 2027 (NJSBA Family Law Symposium pattern, New Brunswick), February 2027 (NJSBA Solo and Small-Firm Conference pattern, New Brunswick), May 2027 (NJSBA Annual Meeting and NJAA Conference & Expo), June 2027 (PIANJ/PIANY), October 2027 (Big I NJ Agents Conference) - and confirm each with the association, since only the 2026 dates are published.

pitfalls.pitfall: Buying a premium vendor membership before having a sellable offer: NJRHA's top tier is $12,500 and NJ ACCA's is $14,000, both payable annually, for a consultancy with no clients yet.

Assuming you can just walk a trade show floor: NJAA states plainly that non-member suppliers and vendors cannot attend its Conference & Expo, so travel and time can be wasted without the supplier membership first.

Treating the state bar association as a membership you can join: the NJSBA application admits attorneys, out-of-state attorneys and legal professionals such as paralegals and legal administrators, not outside technology consultants - so budget for exhibitor/sponsor fees instead of dues.

Confusing the two 'NJSBA' organizations (the New Jersey State Bar Association at njsba.com and the New Jersey School Boards Association at njsba.org / workshop.njsba.org) and registering for or sponsoring the wrong annual convention.

Paying for a booth in a hall already full of legal-tech vendors: the NJSBA Annual Meeting previous-exhibitor list includes Clio, Smokeball, PracticePanther, LEAP, FindLaw, Anytime AI and DRai Solutions, so a generic 'AI agents' booth will read as undifferentiated.

Missing the print and sponsor deadlines: CAI-NJ ad space closes on the 15th of the prior month, NJSBA annual meeting applications after its December cutoff require full payment up front, and NJAA sponsorship inventory is finite (3 breakfasts, 4 lunches).

Assuming 2026 dates repeat: the 2027 dates were not posted on the pages opened during this research (NJSBA annual meeting, NJRHA, PHCC NJ/PA), so calendar assumptions should be verified before booking travel.

Joining the wrong HVAC association: NJ ACCA states that it and national ACCA are separate and that membership in one does not grant membership in the other, so dues paid to one buy no access to the other's events or lists.

Treating an undated association page as current: CAI-NJ's FAQ still prints a 2020 booth-sale schedule and Big I NJ's new-member application is still headed 2018-2019, so both dues and booth mechanics should be re-confirmed in writing before paying.

caveats: All prices are as published at the time of research (November 12, 2026) and several reflect the 2026 program year; 2027 rate cards for NJSBA, NJAA, CAI-NJ partnerships and NJRHA were not yet published.

The Big I NJ 2026 NJ Agents Conference (October 18-20, 2026) and the 2026 NJSBA events described here have already occurred; they are cited as evidence of format, pricing and audience, not as upcoming dates.
The PIANJ/PIANY schedule page does not print a year; the June 7-9 window is inferred to be 2026 because June 7 falls on a Sunday in 2026, matching the listed 'Sunday, June 7'.
Association membership dues for the buyers themselves (agencies, firms, restaurants) are context only; the consultancy would buy associate/vendor/sponsor categories, which are priced separately.

Big I NJ's agency dues schedule ($680-$3,955) comes from an application form still headed 2018-2019, so it is rated Medium and should be treated as a direction of travel rather than a current quote; the current agency membership page publishes the discounts but no dues table.
CAI-NJ's FAQ answers on directory listings and booth priority are undated and sit beside a 2020 booth-sale schedule, so they are rated Medium.
The NJAA sponsorship brochure is member-gated; only the individually published sponsorship line items in the 2026 PDF could be verified, and no booth price is stated in any page opened here.
No first-hand founder accounts or survey data on ROI from these channels were found; all channel economics here are published rate cards, not measured conversion.
data_gaps: Middlesex County Bar Association (mcbalaw.com) returned HTTP 403 to every request, including its membership, events and bar-sponsor pages; its dues, event calendar and sponsorship prices could not be verified and are omitted rather than cited from search snippets.

CAI-NJ 2027 Partnership Program pricing: the chapter's 2027 partnership page rendered only navigation, and the 2026 partnership PDF URL returned 404; tier prices (reported elsewhere as $3,850/$7,150/$11,000 for 2026) could not be confirmed on a page opened during this research.
NJAA Conference & Expo booth pricing and the full sponsorship brochure require a member login, so only the individually published sponsorship items ($500-$750) are stated.
New Jersey Food Council membership dues are not published; the site directs inquiries to 609-392-8899 / njfc@njfoodcouncil.com, and the sponsor page shows no prices.

PHCC New Jersey: dues are not shown on the public sign-up page, the chapter event calendar rendered as an empty month grid, and the national PHCC event page returned no body text - so neither NJ PHCC dues nor the 2027 NJ/PA convention date could be verified.

PIANJ dues and exhibitor booth pricing: the only rate document found was a December 2023 application PDF on a static host, too old to cite as current 2026-27 pricing, and the schedule page lists no exhibit fees.

NJSBA 2027 dates: the official annual meeting page says planning is underway with no dates; a May 19-21, 2027 reference appeared only in search results and was not confirmed on a page opened here. The 2027 Solo and Small-Firm Conference and Family Law Symposium dates were likewise not posted.
Middlesex County Regional Chamber of Commerce dues: the 2024 membership application PDF returned an empty document and the chamber's sponsorship page lists no prices.

No published attendance counts were found for the NJSBA Solo and Small-Firm Conference, the Family Law Symposium, the PIANJ/PIANY trade show, or NJAA's expo floor beyond the NJRHA ProStart figure of about 150 attendees.
